text:
Maya: Heads-up — saw two overlapping spot interruption waves in us-west2 starting ~08:10 UTC, caused lots of routing churn. Hosted API 95p latency up ~30% during flaps. Anyone on call can triage and propose fast mitigations?
Sam: grabbing dashboards now — looks correlated with a wave of preemptions from the cloud provider (batch of preemptible VMs reclaimed). link: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/spot_preemptions
InfraBot: ALERT: spot_preempt_rate(us-west2) = 0.118 > threshold 0.05; auto-fallbacks triggered: 18 requests routed to dedicated-pool-1, 42 to fallback-models.
Ryan: Quick idea — implement a preemptive-shuffle policy: when preempt rate > 5% for 2m, proactively mark low-priority spot instances as "draining" and shift new requests to (a) other regions with capacity, (b) dedicated reserved pools for enterprise customers, (c) model-variant fallback (quantized smaller model) for non-critical traffic.
Katie: +1. Need to be careful with cross-region egress costs and latency for user sessions pinned to region. Can we do model-variant fallback first (cheap), then region failover for non-enterprise?
Sam: I like: 1) model_variant fallback (soft degrade), 2) route enterprise -> dedicated if available, 3) region failover last. Also add a short TTL on routing decisions so we don't thrash.
Dmitri: Patching the runtime routing table should be trivial. Proposed rule (pseudo-yaml):
```
when: spot_preempt_rate(region) > 0.05 for 120s
actions:
  - apply_model_fallback: {traffic_fraction: 0.25, target_variant: "small-quant"}
  - reroute_by_tier: {enterprise: dedicated_pool, standard: prefer_other_region}
  - set_ttl: 300s
```
Sam: We'll also want to enable a 5% canary shift first to validate quality impact on prompts/evals.
Maya: Who takes ownership to implement canary + rollout? I can coordinate QA/evals.
Ryan: I can own the routing rule and runtime patch, Dmitri can handle draining logic for spot VMs.
Dmitri: I'll add a small controller to watch node preemption signals and initiate a graceful drain: `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`. Will also annotate pods with `preempt-shuffle=true` so runtime avoids them for new prefixes.
Eli: Cross-region egress estimate: if 20% traffic shifts to e.g. us-east, rough monthly delta $3.4k at current rates. Approve one-off 24h runway?
Katie: Finance thumbs-up for triage window. Long term we need a cost guardrail to auto-disable region failover for low-margin customers.
Sam: Also add metric: routing_fallback_rate and model_quality_regressions tied to prompt-set so we can auto-rollback if quality drops > 2% on key prompts.
Maya: Agreed. Let's run canary (5%) for 30m, measure latency, error rate, and quality delta. If OK, expand to 25% for 1h, then full policy. Rollback on quality regression >2% or error spike >1%.
InfraBot: ACTION: created ticket INFRA-4723 "preemptive shuffle + model-fallback canary" assigned to Ryan/Dmitri, due in 4h.
Sam: Quick commands to run canary route (runtime CLI):
```
runtime route apply --policy preemptive-shuffle-v1 --canary 0.05 --regions us-west2,us-east1
```
Ryan: I'll deploy `preemptive-shuffle-v1` now to canary. Pinging @Katie for QA hooks and @Eli for cost monitor.
Katie: I'll seed the eval set and run automated comparisons.
Dmitri: Draining controller PR up: https://git.internal/p/1234 review pls.
Maya: Thanks team. If the canary looks good, we'll schedule an automated rollback job to revert policy after 24h if any thresholds crossed. Meeting in 15m for quick sync. :thumbsup:
